message.content: The number of mitochondria varies widely among cell types and conditions, but a typical mammalian cell contains roughly **hundreds to thousands** of mitochondria (often cited as ~200–2,000 per cell). Cells with high energy demands—such as muscle or nerve cells—can have even more, while other cell types may contain fewer.
